statement: Section 4 decides only the container's shape; byte offsets, field widths and the serialisation encoding are explicitly not specified there and are deferred to §25.
research_needed: Prototype candidate encodings (fixed-width vs varint, canonical serialisation) and measure parse robustness, size and fuzz resistance.
decision_needed: What byte offsets, field widths and serialisation encoding does ECF use?

statement: Manifest-first, footer-indexed, record-oriented and hybrid designs are treated as one format: the manifest is a sequence of records, and a single declared layout field (STREAM or INDEXED) determines where the records sit.
STREAM layout emits manifest records inline, immediately after the chunk data they describe, so the archive can be produced by a process that never seeks and never knows the total size in advance.
research_needed: Conformance test packing from unseekable input to a pipe: confirm no seeks and a valid, verifiable archive.

statement: INDEXED layout keeps manifest records contiguous in one section with an Index section mapping entries and chunks to byte ranges; random access is claimed to be O(1) after two range reads.
research_needed: Measure range-request count and latency per entry access over HTTP, including index validation against authority (§4.5) and encrypted manifests (§4.7).

statement: Each manifest record appears exactly once (I19); unlike ZIP's local header plus central directory, ECF holds no duplicate copies of the same facts, and the layout field only says where records are.
research_needed: Differential/fuzz tests confirming no field is derivable from two physical locations.

statement: `entrybound repack --layout=indexed` moves manifest records without duplicating them and without changing logical identity (§8.1).
research_needed: Round-trip STREAM->INDEXED->STREAM tests asserting LAI equality and single-occurrence of records.

statement: A STREAM-layout archive is fully valid and fully verifiable; it simply costs O(n) to reach entry n, and repack is the stated remedy.
research_needed: Demonstrate single-pass full verification (budgets, digests, signatures, Merkle) of STREAM archives.

statement: Because repack preserves logical identity, a signature made over a STREAM archive is claimed to still verify over its INDEXED form.
research_needed: Formal check that signatures bind only layout-independent identity roots; security review of which physical-layer bytes (layout, index, framing) are thereby unsigned and attacker-malleable.
decision_needed: Which archive fields are covered by signatures, and is an unsigned physical layer acceptable?

statement: Every parser differential in ZIP's history is said to live in the gap between the local header and central directory, two copies of the same facts.
research_needed: Classify documented ZIP parser differentials/CVEs to confirm or bound the word 'every'.

statement: The preamble is a fixed-size structure at offset 0 holding twelve ordered items: magic, format version, feature bitmaps, bitmap checksum, layout, DecodeRequirements, ResourceBudget, BudgetDeclared, archive role, stream_dedup_window, collision/hostility summary, footer locator hint.
decision_needed: What is the fixed preamble size, and how can fixed-size fields accommodate future growth?

statement: Preamble item 1 is an 8-byte magic number, specified in §18.3.
research_needed: Check candidate magic against libmagic/file(1) databases for collisions.
decision_needed: Confirm the 8-byte magic sequence chosen in §18.3.

statement: The preamble carries a major/minor format version; a reader rejects an unknown major version immediately.
The preamble carries three-tier feature bitmaps: incompat, ro_compat and compat (§20.1).
decision_needed: What bitmap widths and bit assignments are used?

statement: A checksum over the feature bitmaps lets a reader distinguish a corrupt preamble from unsupported features (I21), generalising the xz flags-CRC refinement.
decision_needed: Which checksum algorithm protects the feature bitmaps (and is it the whole preamble or bitmaps only)?

statement: The source asserts that no archive format currently checksums its feature flags to distinguish corrupt from unsupported (xz, a compression stream format, is cited as the model).
research_needed: Survey zip, tar, 7z, RAR5, xz, zstd, squashfs, WIM, DwarFS header designs for flag checksums.

statement: The preamble declares the layout: STREAM or INDEXED.
Preamble DecodeRequirements declares maximum window size, maximum working-set memory, and whether any declared feature requires an unusual decoder capability.
research_needed: Validate that writers can compute conservative working-set memory for every codec/transform/lookback combination.
decision_needed: What counts as an 'unusual decoder capability' and how is it encoded?

statement: DecodeRequirements are archive-wide maxima, while window and memory choices are made per chunk group; whether per-group requirements are also declared, so a constrained reader can decode the subset it can afford, is not stated.
decision_needed: Are decode requirements declared only archive-wide or also per group/section?

statement: Preamble ResourceBudget declares eight upper bounds: entry count, total logical bytes, maximum single-entry logical bytes, maximum expansion ratio, maximum chunk count, maximum path depth, maximum metadata bytes, maximum key-derivation cost.
research_needed: Corpus analysis of real archives to set reader default policy budgets; check legitimate high expansion ratios (dedup of zeros, sparse files).
decision_needed: What field widths/units apply (e.g., expansion ratio representation, KDF cost unit), and what reader default budgets pair with them?

statement: Maximum key-derivation cost is a declared budget field because a stored, attacker-supplied KDF cost is a denial-of-service vector; merely reporting it (§9.11) is not refusing it.
research_needed: Security review of password-KDF DoS; benchmark Argon2id parameter ranges on low-end hardware.
decision_needed: How are Argon2id memory, iterations and parallelism normalised into one bounded budget value, and what default reader ceiling applies?

statement: An unnamed proprietary format already bounds key-derivation count (its one axis of specification superiority); zstd declares only a window size; ZIP and tar declare nothing.
research_needed: Identify the proprietary format and verify its KDF bound; confirm zstd/ZIP/tar declaration facts.

statement: The preamble carries a BudgetDeclared flag; a producer writing to a pipe from an unseekable source cannot know the eight budget values and sets BudgetDeclared = false.
The preamble declares the archive role (Complete, Sidecar, Incremental; §8.5) so a reader can refuse a non-extractable archive before doing anything.
The preamble carries stream_dedup_window, which in STREAM layout bounds a single-pass reader's chunk cache (§4.6).
The preamble carries a collision and hostility class summary naming which P5 and P8 classes are present, so a caller can refuse before extracting.
decision_needed: How is the class summary encoded, and which fixed taxonomy of classes does it enumerate?

statement: The offset-0 preamble must state DecodeRequirements and the collision/hostility summary before payload, but a single-pass writer with unseekable input cannot know them in advance; only ResourceBudget has a stated undeclared fallback.
evidence_in_source: inference: no fallback stated in source
research_needed: Design review of a single-pass writer listing which preamble items are knowable a priori.
decision_needed: What does a single-pass writer write for DecodeRequirements and the hostility summary when unknown, and how is 'unknown' encoded and reported?

statement: Preamble item 12 is a footer locator hint that is advisory only; the footer is self-locating and the hint must not be trusted.

Preamble and ArchiveDescriptor are one logical object in two places: the fixed preamble holds items 1-12 needed before allocation; a footer-located ArchiveDescriptor section holds identity roots, layout details, identity-profile ID, planner ID and chunker version.
The ArchiveDescriptor is called a footer-located section and STREAM_BODY is introduced as a section, yet the §4.3 section-type list contains neither type.
decision_needed: Are ARCHIVE_DESCRIPTOR and STREAM_BODY distinct section types, and what is the complete section-type registry?

statement: The preamble declares upper bounds and the footer reports actual totals; being different facts they do not violate I19. Where a bound is present the actual must not exceed it, and a reader finding otherwise aborts.

§4.2 says the footer reports actual totals, but §4.4 lists footer contents as trailer magic, total length, descriptor/manifest locators and a preamble-binding digest, and says the footer holds locators, not facts.
decision_needed: Where are actual totals (entry count, logical bytes, chunk count, etc.) recorded: footer, descriptor, or manifest?

statement: With BudgetDeclared = false the reader enforces only its own policy budget (§11.5), which the source claims is sufficient for safety but forfeits O(1) pre-refusal.
research_needed: Test that reader policy budgets alone stop decompression bombs and entry explosions in undeclared archives with bounded memory.

statement: `inspect` and `unpack` must report an archive as having an undeclared budget; silence would violate I25.
Even with an undeclared budget, actuals are still reported, so a second pass or a repack yields a fully-declared archive.

Budget declaration is conditional: producers that can stat their input (e.g., `pack ./dir` piped to ssh) declare bounds despite pipe output; only producers whose input is also unseekable leave the budget undeclared.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects an earlier draft that claimed budget declaration was unconditional (§4.2 L399)

statement: A producer that stats the tree first to declare bounds may see files grow or appear before reading; the source does not say what happens when actuals would exceed an already-written bound on pipe output.
research_needed: Pack tests against concurrently mutating trees to pipe output.
decision_needed: Should writers add slack to bounds, exclude offending files, or fail when mid-pack growth would exceed a declared bound on unseekable output?

statement: DecodeRequirements plus ResourceBudget are the format-level answer to decompression bombs, entry-count explosions and memory exhaustion; no incumbent archive format is said to declare more than one of them.
research_needed: Incumbent survey (zip, tar, 7z, RAR5, xz, zstd, squashfs, WIM, DwarFS, OCI) plus bomb-corpus tests against Entrybound readers.

statement: Declared budgets are untrusted claims that must be consistent: a reader compares them with its policy budget and refuses before allocating, and validates during decode, failing when reality exceeds the claim, so a lying archive is caught either way.
research_needed: Fuzzing with lying budgets; confirm detection occurs before exceeding the claim by more than a bounded slack.

statement: The body is a sequence of self-describing sections, each carrying a type, a length and a digest of its own contents; traversal is by length field with no padding (the DwarFS shape).
decision_needed: Which digest algorithm and length width apply to section framing?

statement: Per-section digests are claimed to make a damaged section localisable without a full scan.
research_needed: Corruption-injection experiments measuring localisation, including damage to a length field that breaks traversal of all later sections.

statement: Section framing has no padding, yet §4.7/§9.8 contemplate padding to hide the chunk size sequence; the slice does not say where privacy padding resides or whether alignment padding (e.g., for mmap) is ever permitted.
decision_needed: Where does privacy padding live given padding-free section framing, and is any alignment padding allowed?

statement: Section types are MANIFEST_RECORDS, CHUNK_DATA, DICTIONARY, TRANSFORM_PLANS, METADATA, FIDELITY, INDEX, CRYPTO_ENVELOPE, SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD and MERKLE_OUTBOARD.
decision_needed: How are section type IDs assigned and extended, and how are unknown section types handled?

statement: INDEX is the only section a conforming reader may ignore entirely.

If only INDEX is ignorable, a conforming reader must process SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD and MERKLE_OUTBOARD, which strains minimal/independent readers and compat-tier optional features; per-section reader obligations are not stated.
decision_needed: What must a minimal conforming reader do with SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD, MERKLE_OUTBOARD and compat-feature sections?

statement: A fixed-size, self-locating footer at file end holds a trailer magic, total container length, offsets and lengths of the descriptor and manifest sections, and a digest binding the footer to the preamble.
decision_needed: What are the exact footer size, field set and binding digest algorithm?

statement: One unconditional range request locates everything, copying the pattern production random-access formats converged on: eStargz 51-byte footer, zstd-seekable 9-byte footer, zstd:chunked 64-byte trailer.
evidence_in_source: cited prior-art sizes; no primary citation in slice
research_needed: Verify cited footer sizes against specifications; measure total range requests for remote list and single-entry extract.

statement: Truncation must be detectable and distinguishable by comparing declared total length with actual file length, reporting that the archive is truncated at N bytes with entries 1..k intact.

Truncation removes the footer carrying the declared total length and manifest locators; the slice does not explain how a reader learns the declared length or identifies intact entries 1..k, especially in INDEXED layout where the manifest section may be lost.
research_needed: Truncation corpus at every offset for both layouts; measure what is recoverable and reportable.
decision_needed: What mechanism (preamble length, STREAM scan, per-record digests) supports truncation reports when the footer is missing?

statement: Truncation is asserted to be the dominant real-world failure for archives, and no incumbent is said to handle it well.
research_needed: Failure-mode data (bug trackers, download-corruption studies) and truncation behaviour tests of incumbent tools.

statement: The footer cannot contradict the preamble because it is bound to it by digest and contains only locators, not facts.
I10 operationally: the Index section must be fully reconstructible from the manifest records and chunk table.
A conforming implementation ships an `entrybound repack --rebuild-index` path.
The conformance corpus (§19.3) contains archives with deliberately wrong indexes, and a conforming reader must produce identical output on them as on their corrected twins.
A reader validates any index-derived value against the authority (manifest records and chunk table) before use.

Validating every index-derived value against the manifest authority may require reading manifest records or chunk frames, which could undermine the claimed O(1)-after-two-range-reads random access, especially remotely.
research_needed: Measure remote random-access cost with full index validation; evaluate per-record digests or Merkle proofs as validation granularity.
decision_needed: What validation suffices to trust an index value without a full manifest read?

statement: RAR5's quick open record is a cache readers may trust, and the RAR specification warns that displaying from it requires extracting from it, i.e., a parser differential written into a specification; index-as-cache is called the key ZIP-corpus lesson.
research_needed: Primary citation of the RAR5 technote wording.

statement: ZIP general-purpose bit 3 data descriptors, which create a second size authority, occur in 15.9% of real published ZIP artifacts according to the Research III measurement.
research_needed: Confirm corpus definition, sample size and reproducibility of the 15.9% figure.

statement: An entry's logical facts are written once, after its data, in the entry's own manifest record, so there is no forward declaration to contradict.
A STREAM body is one alternation of items, each starting with a one-byte item tag: 0x01 CHUNK_FRAME (stored_len, flags{end_of_content}, stored bytes) and 0x02 MANIFEST_RECORD (record_len, record).
refines_or_supersedes: Narrows the §4 L353 deferral of byte-level detail by fixing tag values

statement: Encodings of stored_len, record_len and the flags field, and reader behaviour on an unknown item tag (extensibility beyond 0x01/0x02), are unspecified.
decision_needed: What length encodings are used, and must readers reject or skip unknown item tags?

statement: An item tag is required because entries emitting no chunk frames are common (directories, zero-length files, fully deduplicated entries when stream_dedup_window > 0); the reader dispatches on the tag rather than guessing and desynchronising.
stored_len is declared only in the chunk frame; the manifest record does not restate it and the index only caches it (I10, I19), avoiding the ZIP data-descriptor defect class.

An end_of_content flag marks the last frame of the current ContentObject so a reader knows where content ends without a forward count; the chunk count appears exactly once, in the following manifest record.

Reader loop: read a tag; on CHUNK_FRAME read the frame and bytes noting end_of_content; on MANIFEST_RECORD read the record, which names and types whatever frames preceded it (possibly none), then act.

Only two item tags exist, yet archives carry dictionaries, transform plans, metadata, fidelity report, signatures, conversion records and Merkle outboard; the slice does not say how these appear in a single-pass STREAM_BODY or whether they are available before chunks needing them.
decision_needed: Where do DICTIONARY, TRANSFORM_PLANS, METADATA, FIDELITY, SIGNATURES, CONVERSION_RECORD and MERKLE_OUTBOARD live in STREAM layout?

statement: The relation between a CHUNK_FRAME and chunk groups with declared lookback is unstated: whether a frame holds one chunk or a group's compressed stream, and how a manifest record references earlier-emitted deduplicated chunks, is unspecified.
decision_needed: Is a CHUNK_FRAME a chunk or a chunk group, and do records reference prior chunks by chunk_id or by position?

statement: In STREAM layout the body is one STREAM_BODY section whose length is written in the footer rather than at its head, containing the tagged item sequence; in INDEXED layout the body uses the typed sections of §4.3.
refines_or_supersedes: Refines §4.3 L407 (sections carry their length at the head)

statement: The footer locates either a contiguous MANIFEST_RECORDS section (INDEXED) or the STREAM_BODY plus a reconstructed record offset table (STREAM, after repack or index build); the layout field decides, so no reader infers it.

For a freshly streamed archive without an index build, it is unclear what the footer's manifest locator points to, where a record offset table or INDEX lives when the body is one section, and whether adding one keeps STREAM layout.
decision_needed: What does the STREAM-layout footer contain before and after an index build, and does an index build keep STREAM layout or convert to INDEXED?

statement: When BudgetDeclared = false, max_chunk_count is absent and the frame sequence is bounded by the caller's policy budget; I20 is met by policy rather than declaration, and inspect reports which bound applied.

A STREAM-layout archive declares stream_dedup_window, the maximum distance in chunks between a chunk's physical position and any reference to it, so a single-pass reader's cache is bounded and declared rather than dictated by the dedup pattern.
Default stream_dedup_window is zero for pipe output (dedup within a ContentObject only); for seekable output the writer defaults to unbounded dedup.
research_needed: Measure dedup ratio lost at window 0 versus bounded windows on streaming workloads (CI artifacts, backups, container layers).
decision_needed: Is zero the right pipe default, or should a bounded non-zero window be the default?

statement: Writer default layout follows the output: seekable output defaults to INDEXED layout; pipe output is STREAM layout.

The dedup window is measured in chunks while reader cache memory scales with chunk bytes; and a window of zero is said to allow dedup within a ContentObject, which a strict chunk-distance of zero would forbid.
decision_needed: Is stream_dedup_window denominated in chunks or bytes, and does 0 mean no cross-object references or no back-references at all?

statement: Encrypted archives require INDEXED layout in v1, because encrypting the whole manifest as one unit is impossible when records interleave with chunk data.
A per-record encryption scheme would leak record boundaries and therefore entry count and approximate name lengths.
research_needed: Leakage analysis of per-record encryption with and without padding, to inform the deferred encrypted STREAM design.

statement: `pack --recipient` to a pipe either buffers to a temporary file or fails with an explanation of the INDEXED-only restriction.
research_needed: Security review of temporary-file exposure and disk-space failure behaviour.
decision_needed: Does pack --recipient to a pipe buffer or fail by default, where is the temp file, and can it contain plaintext?

statement: v1 will not ship a weaker encrypted-streaming mode and describe it as equivalent to whole-manifest encryption.
Encrypted STREAM layout is a §25 deferral.
research_needed: Design and leakage analysis of streaming encryption that hides record boundaries.
decision_needed: Will Entrybound ever support encrypted STREAM layout, and with what leakage bound?

statement: A streaming reader learns an entry's name after its bytes, so extraction writes to a temporary object and renames it, as a safe extractor does anyway (§11.6).
research_needed: Platform feasibility: temp object placement inside the confined destination, rename semantics on Windows/NTFS ADS and special files, cleanup on failure.

statement: Accepted residual STREAM costs: post-hoc entry naming during extraction and `list` requiring a full pass; repack removes both.

An encrypted archive encrypts the entire manifest, metadata, index and fidelity report as one unit; only the preamble, the CryptoEnvelope (recipient stanzas, suite identifiers, commitment) and section framing needed to find them are public.

The public preamble declares ResourceBudget bounds (entry count, path depth, metadata and logical bytes), archive role and collision/hostility summary, contradicting §4.7's claim that entry count and structure disappear; the stated residue lists only size, recipient count and chunk sizes.
research_needed: Formal enumeration of every public field in an encrypted archive.
decision_needed: Are budget and hostility fields encrypted, coarsened or omitted in encrypted archives, and is the §9.8 leakage list complete?

statement: The one-unit encryption list omits DICTIONARY, TRANSFORM_PLANS, CONVERSION_RECORD, SIGNATURES and MERKLE_OUTBOARD; plaintext-derived Merkle digests or plans left public would enable content confirmation or category leakage.
research_needed: Security review of confirmation-of-file and category leakage from each unlisted section.
decision_needed: Which remaining section types are encrypted, and do plaintext-addressed digests (I28) ever appear in the clear?

statement: Encrypting manifest and index as one AEAD unit implies decrypting and holding the whole manifest for any access, straining O(1) remote random access and bounded memory for archives with millions of entries.
research_needed: Measure memory and latency of single-unit manifest decryption at 1M-10M entries versus segmented online AEAD.
decision_needed: Is 'one unit' a single AEAD call or a segmented/online AEAD over metadata sections?

statement: gocryptfs and CryFS pay heavily to hide filenames and structure because they expose a live tree; CryFS's directory flattening is cited as costing a measured 4x on extraction workloads.
evidence_in_source: cited measurement; no primary citation in slice
research_needed: Locate the primary source of the 4x figure.

statement: Hiding filenames, directory structure, entry count, per-entry metadata and the fidelity report is claimed to be nearly free: one AEAD operation over a section written anyway.
research_needed: Benchmark encrypted versus unencrypted pack, list and extract overhead.

statement: Encrypted archives leave visible only total archive size, recipient count and, unless padding is enabled, the chunk size sequence; §9.8 enumerates this.
research_needed: Leakage analysis of CDC chunk-size sequences (I24 attack literature) and padding schedule efficacy.
decision_needed: Is padding enabled by default for encrypted archives?

statement: From the preamble alone, before any allocation, a reader determines format version, every required, read-only-compatible and optional feature, and the decode requirements; it never parses content to learn whether it can parse content (§20).
In unencrypted archives the manifest is not compressed by default, trading some space for Library of Congress transparency: running strings on an .eb reveals entry names.
research_needed: Measure uncompressed versus compressed manifest overhead across entry-count scales.

statement: A `compact-manifest` feature exists for archives with millions of entries and is an incompat feature, so nothing silently loses transparency.
research_needed: Manifest size and parse cost at 1M+ entries.
decision_needed: When does the writer enable compact-manifest, and what encoding or codec does it use?

statement: A conforming decoder for the baseline codec set must be small, with an explicit budget in §20.6; the 2026 AIT data-compression challenge's 1 MB decompressor limit is cited as the right instinct.
research_needed: Measure decoder code size for candidate baseline codecs and a minimal reader.
decision_needed: What numeric decoder size budget does §20.6 set?

statement: The specification must be normative, versioned and archived, and the conformance corpus ships with it (§19.3).
PNG's 1996 byte sequence is cited as bit-identical in its 2025 W3C Recommendation, while GNU tar sparse formats 0.0 and 0.1, specified only by implementation, are said to be unreadable outside GNU.
evidence_in_source: cited historical observation; no primary citation in slice
research_needed: Verify against primary sources, including whether libarchive/bsdtar read GNU sparse 0.0/0.1.

statement: No external dependency is structural for a Complete archive: no network service, key server or registry lookup is required to decode a Complete archive you hold.
research_needed: Offline decode conformance test; separate decode dependencies from signature/timestamp trust validation.

statement: Sidecar and Incremental roles depend on external content by definition; the role is declared in the preamble and participates in identity so the dependency is never a surprise.

Three-tier evolution: a v1.4 reader safely reads a v1.7 archive using only compat features, read-only-accesses one using ro_compat features, and cleanly refuses one using an unknown incompat feature with a message naming the feature (§20).

'Read-only' is ill-defined for immutable archives (does ro_compat forbid repack, append, recipient mutation, re-signing?), and an old reader cannot name an unknown feature except by bit or identifier.
decision_needed: Which operations does ro_compat forbid for archives, and how is an unknown feature named in refusal messages?

statement: The planner is a creation-time policy engine assigning a TransformPlan to every chunk group; it is neither a compression algorithm nor part of the decoder, and its whole output is data recorded in the archive.
The decoder never knows a planner existed; it reads plans. This makes planner evolution free (§5.7) and profiles a creation-time-only concept (§6).
The planner pipeline is Scan, Categorise, Chunk, Deduplicate, Cluster, Group, Plan, Verify, Emit.
Scan walks the input, captures metadata (§10) and records fidelity gaps.
Categorise assigns each region a content category by inspecting bytes, never by file extension.
research_needed: Accuracy of byte-based detection on real corpora; effects of adversarial mis-categorisation on ratio and resource use.

statement: Category incompressible, detected by a fast entropy/compressibility probe, is stored and skips all further analysis.
research_needed: Measure probe false-positive/negative rates and throughput.
decision_needed: Which probe and threshold classify a region as incompressible?

statement: 'Skip all further analysis' for incompressible regions conflicts with dedup being always on; whether incompressible data (media, encrypted blobs) is still content-defined-chunked and deduplicated is unstated.
decision_needed: Are incompressible regions still CDC-chunked and deduplicated?

statement: Category already-compressed-container, detected by format signature (zip, gz, png, jpeg, ...), makes content a candidate for reconstruction transforms (§5.5).
research_needed: Measure prevalence and net gain of reconstruction on real corpora.

statement: Category executable plus architecture, from ELF/PE/Mach-O headers per architecture and per slice for fat binaries, selects an instruction filter for that architecture.
research_needed: Measure branch-converter filter gains per architecture; define slice detection.

statement: Category text/source, detected by byte distribution and ASCII ratio, is a dictionary candidate with strong context modelling.
Category structured-numeric, detected by regular record width and float patterns, is planned with byte-shuffle, stream-split or delta.
research_needed: Record-width detection accuracy and measured gains.

statement: Category media, detected by format signature, receives a format-specific reversible transform where one exists.
research_needed: Inventory bit-exact reversible media transforms and their gains.

statement: Category model-weights, detected by safetensors/GGUF signatures and BF16/FP16 patterns, is planned with a sign/exponent/mantissa split.
research_needed: Measure gains versus plain codecs on real checkpoints; confirm the split is invertible over arbitrary bytes.

statement: Category unknown is the default and triggers a generic codec search.

The categoriser is modelled on one unnamed production system that recognises ELF, PE and Mach-O with architecture subcategories and applies per-category compression, ordering, window and lookback settings.
research_needed: Identify the system and verify its measured benefit.

statement: The granularity of a categorised region (file, fat-binary slice, embedded stream) is undefined, and because categories drive per-category chunking the categoriser must itself be pinned for determinism; neither is stated.
decision_needed: What is a region, and is the categoriser version pinned by the planner ID and chunker version?

statement: Chunking uses content-defined chunking with per-category parameters (§7).
research_needed: Measure dedup and ratio across CDC parameter choices per category.
decision_needed: What CDC parameters apply per category?

statement: Per-category CDC parameters give identical bytes different boundaries when categorised differently (e.g., the same data embedded in different file types), reducing cross-file dedup and making PCR sensitive to categoriser decisions.
research_needed: Measure cross-category dedup loss versus a single global parameter set.
decision_needed: Should CDC parameters be global, per category, or per profile?

statement: Exact chunk deduplication by chunk_id is always on and never disabled; its reach is declared, and in STREAM layout reference distance is bounded by stream_dedup_window (zero for pipe output).

Always-on dedup inside encrypted archives exposes repeated-content structure through chunk counts and sizes; given the I24 CDC-attack literature, whether dedup or CDC behaviour must change under encryption is not addressed in this slice.
research_needed: Security analysis of dedup plus CDC leakage under encryption.
decision_needed: Must dedup or CDC behaviour change when encryption is enabled?

statement: Cluster performs similarity grouping (min-hash / nilsimsa class) to place similar chunks near each other so a long window or shared dictionary can exploit them.
research_needed: Measure ratio gain versus CPU and memory cost.
decision_needed: Which similarity algorithm and parameters are used?

statement: Clustering adds no cluster object to the format but has format-visible outcomes: ordering sets adjacency, adjacency sets grouping, grouping sets stored size and access granularity; the clustering seed is fixed by the planner ID.

Cluster, Group and cross-file Plan steps need a global view of chunks, conflicting with single-pass STREAM output from unknown input and with bounded writer memory for inputs larger than RAM; no streaming or bounded-memory planner is described.
research_needed: Measure planner memory versus input size; design windowed planning.
decision_needed: How does the planner operate in STREAM layout and when input exceeds RAM?

statement: Group assigns chunks to chunk groups with a declared maximum lookback (§7.5), the solid-versus-random-access dial.
For each group the planner searches transform sequence x codec x parameters x dictionary and selects by the profile's objective function (§5.4).
research_needed: Bound search cost; measure ratio gains of search versus fixed choices.

statement: Emit writes sections, computes identities and emits the fidelity report.

Planner inputs include signature and actual content, entropy probes, existing internal compression, repetitiveness and cross-file similarity, CDC boundaries and dedup hit rate, dictionary candidates and training cost, reversible preprocessing, per-arch executable transforms, sampled or full codec evaluation, store decisions, random-access penalty, and CPU and decompression memory.
Decoder window requirement is a planner input: a long-window choice is a decoder-requirement choice that the archive must declare rather than leave to a codec default.
The most common real-world deployment failure with long-window compression is said to be a decoder refusing an archive whose window exceeds its default memory ceiling.
research_needed: Issue-tracker survey of long-window decode failures (e.g., zstd --long).

statement: Transform reconstruction-metadata cost must be weighed: a reconstruction saving 20% but costing 21% in side data is a loss, and only measurement reveals it.
research_needed: Measure correction-stream sizes on real deflate and JPEG corpora.

statement: Parallel-decode structure is a planner input, because grouping decisions determine whether decode parallelises at all.
research_needed: Measure decode scaling versus group layout.

statement: Candidate evaluation 'on sampled data' needs deterministic sample selection, but §5.7 pins only dictionary training samples, dedup iteration and clustering seeds; sampling for probes and codec evaluation is not explicitly pinned.
decision_needed: Is all planner sampling (probes, candidate evaluation) fixed by the planner ID?

statement: A profile is a constrained objective: minimise stored_bytes subject to decompress throughput >= min_decode_rate, decompress memory <= max_decode_memory, random-access granularity <= max_access_granularity, and compress budget <= profile.compress_budget.
decision_needed: What numeric constraint values define each profile (§6)?

statement: decompress_throughput is a machine-dependent rate, yet deterministic mode forbids consulting the environment and requires exact arithmetic; how min_decode_rate is evaluated reproducibly (model or measurement, on what reference) is unspecified.
research_needed: Design a deterministic decode-cost model and validate it against measured throughput across CPUs.
decision_needed: Is decode rate a modelled cost unit or a measured quantity, and how is it pinned?

statement: random_access_granularity is a profile constraint but its unit (bytes per group, chunks per group, lookback distance) is not defined in this slice.
decision_needed: What unit measures random-access granularity?

statement: The extreme profile may not buy ratio with unbounded decode cost: compression time is unbounded, but decode requirements remain declared and bounded (§6.4).

The planner must distinguish three transform classes: Structural (invertible by construction), Reconstructive (bit-exact only if encoder behaviour is reproducible or correctable) and Substitutive (payload preserved, container bytes destroyed).
Structural transforms (instruction filters, delta, byte-shuffle, stream-split) are invertible by construction over arbitrary input; the worst case is only a worse ratio.
research_needed: Property-based and fuzz round-trip tests for each structural transform, including truncated and odd-length inputs.

statement: Round-trip verification is mandated only for reconstructive transforms; structural transforms are unverified on the premise of invertibility, so an implementation bug in a filter could silently corrupt data.
research_needed: Measure the cost of verifying all transformed chunks.
decision_needed: Should writers also round-trip-verify structural transforms, or every chunk?

statement: Reconstructive transforms (deflate-stream reconstruction, JPEG entropy re-coding) are bit-exact only if the encoder's behaviour can be reproduced or corrected; they degrade with larger correction streams or fail on unrecognised encoders.
research_needed: Measure success rate across real encoder populations.

statement: Substitutive transforms that re-encode a stream to a smaller equivalent are prohibited and excluded from Entrybound entirely because they are not bit-exact; §6.5 makes this a contract.
Entrybound's losslessness requires that the original file's bytes survive, not merely the decompressed payload as 'lossless' conventionally means in compression.
No reconstructive transform enters an archive without a verified round-trip; the rule is normative and not negotiable (I31).

For every chunk given a reconstructive transform, the writer decodes its own output and compares it with the original bytes before committing; on mismatch the planner falls back to the next candidate.
Transform fallbacks are recorded in a plan-selection log available via `entrybound explain`.
decision_needed: Is the plan-selection log stored in the archive, in a sidecar, or only available at creation time?

statement: Verification uses the writer's own decoder, so it does not show that other conforming or independent decoders reproduce identical bytes for reconstructive transforms, where decoder divergence is plausible.
research_needed: Differential testing of reconstructive transforms against an independent decoder implementation.
decision_needed: Must registered reconstructive transforms carry test vectors proving cross-decoder determinism?

statement: A production JPEG-XL implementation cannot reliably losslessly recompress JPEGs produced by one common encoder; recompressibility is a per-file, not per-format, property.
evidence_in_source: cited as measured fact; source and encoder unnamed
research_needed: Identify the encoder and reproduce with libjxl.

statement: The safest deflate-reconstruction tool in the field works by verifying and declining rather than predicting.
research_needed: Identify the tool and verify its behaviour and failure rates.

statement: Verification costs one extra decode pass over transformed data, claimed small relative to the compression search, converting an unbounded correctness risk into a bounded, measurable one.
research_needed: Measure verification overhead per profile, especially fast profiles with little search.

statement: Planner IDs are frozen forever: balanced-v1 names one exact behaviour, improvements ship as a new ID (balanced-v2), and an archive records the planner ID that produced it.

Determinism guarantee: identical input bytes, planner ID, declared resource model and pinned encoder versions yield identical TransformPlan sets and chunk boundaries on any machine, core count, available memory or operating system.
research_needed: Cross-platform reproducibility matrix (x86_64/aarch64; Windows/Linux/macOS; 1..N threads; varying memory).

statement: The guarantee covers TransformPlans and chunk boundaries, not whole archive bytes; whether compressed payloads, section order, metadata and (unencrypted) outputs are byte-reproducible is not stated here.
decision_needed: Is full byte-identical archive output guaranteed in deterministic mode for unencrypted archives?

statement: A planner ID pins the version of every encoder in its candidate set, because selection uses measured output size; any encoder change, including bug fixes or ratio improvements, mints a new planner ID.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects an earlier draft that promised frozen planner IDs without pinning third-party encoders (§5.7 L600)

statement: Pinning encoders forces a tool to retain old encoder versions to keep producing old planner IDs, or drop them; handling of security fixes in pinned encoders and planner-ID proliferation is unaddressed.
research_needed: Survey release cadence of candidate encoder crates to estimate planner-ID churn.
decision_needed: Must new releases keep producing old planner IDs, and what happens when a pinned encoder needs a security fix?

statement: In deterministic mode the planner excludes floating-point evaluation (libm differences, FMA contraction, vectorisation) and evaluates its objective in exact integer or fixed-point arithmetic.
research_needed: Audit planner and encoder dependencies for floating-point use that affects decisions.

statement: The design rejects some archival codecs partly for non-portable floating-point behaviour, so consistency forbids a floating-point selector.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to codec rejection decided elsewhere in the design (outside this slice)

statement: In deterministic mode compress_budget is denominated in a deterministic unit (candidate evaluations, bytes examined), never seconds, so the search does not stop at a machine-dependent point.
decision_needed: Which deterministic budget unit(s) and per-profile values are used?

statement: In deterministic mode dedup-table hash/set iteration order, dictionary training sample selection and similarity-clustering seeds are fixed by the planner ID, not the runtime.

Deterministic mode (`--deterministic`, and default for `--profile` with reproducible-build tooling) reads its resource model only from declared values, never the environment, with exact arithmetic, deterministic budgets and fixed orders and seeds.
How the tool detects use 'with reproducible-build tooling' to default into deterministic mode, and which mode is the default otherwise, are unspecified.
decision_needed: What triggers deterministic mode by default, and is adaptive or deterministic the general default?

statement: The declared resource model is load-bearing for determinism, but its fields, whether it is recorded in the archive, and whether a third party can re-derive it to reproduce an archive are unspecified.
decision_needed: What fields constitute the declared resource model, and is it recorded in the archive?

statement: In deterministic mode thread count does not affect output; codec multithreading that changes output bytes is disabled or pinned.
research_needed: Verify output identity across thread counts for each candidate codec.
decision_needed: Is output-changing codec multithreading disabled or pinned?

statement: In adaptive mode the planner may use the real environment; the archive records that it did, and `entrybound verify --reproducible` reports it as adaptively planned rather than failing an unwinnable comparison.
A widely-deployed codec recently switched to multithreaded-by-default, and its multithreaded output is not bit-identical to single-threaded output at the same level.
research_needed: Identify the codec and release and verify the byte differences.

statement: Historical archives are unaffected by planner evolution because plans are data (T1): a later-planner decoder reads an earlier-planner archive with no special case and there is no planner-version compatibility matrix.

No incumbent archive format is said to address files changing under the packer, a real source of silently wrong archives where metadata read, bytes hashed and sparse map queried describe three different file versions.
research_needed: Test incumbents (GNU tar change warnings, bsdtar, 7z, zip) under concurrent modification.

statement: A writer must produce an internally consistent archive or declare that it could not.

One open, one read: each file is opened once and its content, size and metadata are taken from that descriptor; re-stat-ing by path mid-pack is prohibited, as re-resolving a path mid-extraction is (§11.6).
research_needed: Feasibility in safe Rust of handle-based xattr, ACL, ADS and sparse-map queries on Linux, macOS and Windows.

statement: Change detection is mandatory: after reading content the writer re-checks the descriptor's size and modification time, and on change re-reads the file up to a bounded retry count.
research_needed: Test detection on coarse-mtime filesystems (FAT, network shares) and same-size rewrites.
decision_needed: What retry count applies, and are size plus mtime sufficient change signals?

statement: In STREAM layout chunk frames precede the manifest record, so a file found changed after reading cannot be re-read without already-emitted frames remaining in an unseekable stream; retry semantics for pipe output are undefined.
decision_needed: Must STREAM writers buffer whole files before emitting, orphan frames, or mark the entry unstable instead of retrying?

statement: A persistently changing file is either excluded or included with a fidelity.unstable_source record naming it; it is never included silently.
decision_needed: Is the default to exclude the file or include it with an unstable_source record?

statement: Snapshot integration is supported, not required: `pack --snapshot` uses a platform consistent snapshot where available and records it, and the fidelity report states snapshot-consistent versus best-effort.
research_needed: Feasibility and privilege requirements of VSS, APFS, btrfs, ZFS and LVM snapshots from safe Rust.
decision_needed: Which platforms' snapshot mechanisms are supported in v1?

statement: Whether an archive was taken from a consistent view of the tree is a queryable property via `inspect --fidelity`.
Codec and transform identifiers are registries with reserved ranges, not open enumerations.
Every conforming decoder must implement the baseline set, which must be small enough to reimplement (§20.6).

The registered extended set has assigned identifiers, a normative reference, mandatory test vectors and a stated licence, and is declared via incompat features so archives using it fail closed on decoders lacking it.
The experimental range is non-interoperable by construction and may not appear in an archive that claims conformance.
decision_needed: How does an archive claim conformance, and must readers reject experimental identifiers?

statement: The vendor range is namespaced.
decision_needed: What namespacing mechanism does the vendor range use?

statement: Selecting the baseline codec set is a §25 deferral; only the selection criteria are decided in this section.
research_needed: Evaluate candidate codecs and transforms against the five criteria, including decoder size and specification independence.
decision_needed: Which codecs and transforms form the baseline set?

statement: Baseline admission criteria: permissive licence compatible with redistribution; normative format specification independent of any one implementation; published test vectors; bounded, declarable decode memory; and two independent implementations or a spec simple enough to make a second tractable.

A codec whose only specification is its implementation cannot enter the baseline set however good its ratio; strong candidates failing this go to the registered extended set rather than weakening the criterion.
Several strong codec candidates are said to fail the specification-independence test today.
research_needed: Enumerate candidates and check for normative, implementation-independent specifications and independent implementations.

statement: The extended set requires a normative reference, yet codecs specified only by their implementation are routed there; whether a reference implementation may serve as that normative reference is unstated.
decision_needed: Can a reference implementation serve as the normative reference for extended-set registration?
